source.title: WIN-U: Woodbury-Informed Newton-Unlearning as a retain-free Machine Unlearning Framework
source.authors: Xing-Jian Zhao; Mohammad Mohammadi Amiri; Malik Magdon-Ismail

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates benign relearning after unlearning and finds that recovery differs substantially by method: several retain-dependent baselines recover forget-set performance, while MC-WIN-U is more resistant but does not eliminate recovery in every setting.
record.gate_note: Rows record the reported pre/post benign-relearning metrics. The attack fine-tunes unlearned models on the retain set; it does not test relearning on a few examples or a subset of forgotten facts specifically. The paper cites other work about unlearning and suppression, but cited results are not recorded as rows. No ablation, quantization, or prompting-only attack is reported.
record.test_reason: The study applies a benign relearning attack (fine-tuning on the retain set) to five existing unlearning methods and to its own retain-free MC-WIN-U. It reports pre- and post-relearning forget metrics on TOFU, MUSE and WMDP-cyber. These results bear on A (do simple attacks recover unlearned knowledge), B (recovery by fine-tuning on related, non-forget data) and F (whether MC-WIN-U resists the attack). The attack differs from the originals' recipes: it uses the full retain set for 1–3 epochs, so T2. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that retain-dependent baselines show significant forget-information recovery after benign retain-set relearning, which they read as suppression rather than removal. They conclude MC-WIN-U is more robust, often achieving the best post-relearning forget QA probability, and that its utility loss recovers after relearning. They concede the WMDP step size is too aggressive for utility.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes a Woodbury-scaled Newton/Gauss-Newton unlearning method with diagonal-GGN and LoRA approximations; its relearning attack fine-tunes on the retain set. It compares against several existing unlearning methods but does not reproduce one of the listed original-source recipes as its central method.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset/split and unlearning method affect post-relearning outcomes. The paper also reports that MC-WIN-U is sensitive to MC sample count, LoRA rank and step size; no separate numeric row for these settings is included because those ablations do not directly report the relearning attack outcome.

fits_no_version.finding: Unlearning only the WMDP cyber corpus with MC-WIN-U also lowers WMDP-Bio accuracy from 0.668 to 0.600, with MMLU falling 0.592→0.551.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Retain-free Newton-style unlearning causes off-target knowledge loss outside the forget domain.

record.problems: The main recovery attack fine-tunes on the retain set, rather than isolating a few unrelated or loosely related examples. TOFU and MUSE use non-accuracy forget metrics, and no chance levels are reported for them. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates. The WMDP MC-WIN-U run has a large wall-clock cost (50,679s, excluding precomputation), and its authors say the default step size harms utility.
record.rows_left_out: No additional intervention rows left out. Some utility measures for comparison methods and non-relearning benchmark metrics are omitted because they are not needed to capture the relearning outcome or the main general-utility check within the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Only retain-set relearning is tested. No prompting, quantization or activation attacks.
No small or few-example relearning sets: the retain set is large and used for 1–3 epochs. No unrelated data, and no subset of forgotten facts.
Entirely untested: no direction ablation or internal-access analysis.
Entirely untested: no rephrasing, jailbreak, language or in-context attacks.
MC-WIN-U robustness is tested only against retain-set relearning. No activation edits, quantization, prompting or forget-subset relearning.

missing.what: MUSE VerbMem Df pre/post for all methods; MC-WIN-U 0.347→0.573 vs original 0.579
MUSE KnowMem Dr (utility) pre/post; MC-WIN-U 0.429→0.529 vs original 0.555
TOFU forget10 Extraction Strength pre/post; MC-WIN-U 0.085→0.228, RMU 0.054→0.306, GA 0.033→0.393, original 0.701
Original and gold-retrained reference values (TOFU forget prob 0.88–0.90 vs 0.12–0.17) needed to read recovery fraction
Qualitative example: RMU recovers a verbatim answer after 1 epoch; WIN-U does not
Post-relearning forget-retain trade-off across step sizes η

record.verdict_notes: Version codes V1/V2/V6 in the record correspond to A/B/F. The relearning set is the full retain set (large, loosely related data), not a small set. TOFU post values are the worst case across 3 epoch checkpoints. WMDP relearning is 1 epoch. Table 4's text extraction shifts columns: the -99.x values are PrivLeak, not KnowMem Dr. WMDP-Bio is off-target because only cyber was forgotten. Several baselines (SimNPO everywhere; NPO/RMU on WMDP; NPO on MUSE) barely unlearn, so their lack of recovery is uninformative. No seeds or uncertainty are reported. The MC-WIN-U step size η was tuned, and the authors note η selection currently relies on retain-set evaluation.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports forget-set metrics and utility measures, plus relearning outcomes. It does not establish a near-chance criterion for TOFU or MUSE; no chance level is stated for the reported metrics. Its tested relearning attack uses the retain set.

Tests benign fine-tuning on the retain set for 3 epochs on TOFU and MUSE, and 1 epoch on WMDP. It does not test only a few examples, unrelated or loosely related examples as a separately controlled condition, or a subset of forgotten facts.
No activation-direction ablation or direct internal-access mechanism test.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language change, or in-context-information attack.
Tests MC-WIN-U against benign retain-set relearning. Does not test resistance to activation edits, quantization, or prompting-only attacks.
